problem: Which integral gives the area of the finite region bounded by $y=4{x}^{2}-x$ and $y=2-{x}^{2}-4x?$
worked_solution:
First, let's draw a sketch of the two functions.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14013841/assets/913ec93445f3ed571fcf98ad762eba2a1bc657dce7442c8e48fc4d5f36817def.png)

*(Note: Figure not drawn to scale)*

Now, we want to determine the limits of integration. To do this, we equate the two functions and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}4{x}^{2}-x & =2-{x}^{2}-4x \\ 5{x}^{2}+3x-2 & =0 \\ x & =\frac{-3\pm \sqrt{{3}^{2}-4\cdot 5\cdot (-2)}}{2\cdot 5} \\  & =\frac{-3\pm 7}{10}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we need to integrate from $x=-1$ to $x=\frac{2}{5}.$

To determine which is the lower function and which is the upper, let's draw our vertical arrow.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14013841/assets/77493917a13269c78acef8ff6fe57b5f350020542805e316f82f7a17dabedd24.png)

The vertical line 

- *enters* the region through the lower function $y=4{x}^{2}-x,$ and

- *leaves* through the upper function $y=2-{x}^{2}-4x.$

Therefore, the integral that gives our area is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\int }_{-1}^{2/5}[\,(\text{upper function})-(\text{lower function})\,]\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{2/5}[\,(2-{x}^{2}-4x)-(4{x}^{2}-x)\,]\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{2/5}(-5{x}^{2}-3x+2)\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$
